decision.about: How a page says it has data, and what the loaded object may set

options.say: data: true reads <url>page.json; data: { ... } is the same object inline with no fetch; absent means no fetch, no probe, no 404
options.why: one key covers both forms, and the inline POJO needs the same name - json: true would have needed a second key for the object

options.say: json: true, the owner's first wording
options.why: reads well for the file form and has nothing to call the inline form

decision.because: the owner's second dictation asks for the POJO form in the same breath ('rather than json: true you could pass a POJO and put all the data right in there'), so the key has to name the DATA, not the file format. Implemented on the child_source seam the 2026-09-17 data-children work already built, so the file is awaited by load_all_children() before the page renders and before its children are declared, with no new waiting machinery. The file's keys are read through the existing static props() - title, icon, description, the six page words - and merged with ??= so a key the page.js set WINS: the file is the page's data, the page.js is the page's decision, and a generated file must never overwrite a typed line. decision.about: How a directory that holds only a page.json becomes a page

options.why: one more rung, no url pattern; the fetch runs only where a 404 was already the answer, so a page with a module costs exactly what it cost before

options.say: a url pattern or a naming convention that says 'this one is JSON'
options.why: rejected by the owner out loud: 'I do not like a URL pattern to indicate JSON vs page.js'

decision.because: the import above has to fail before the new fetch runs, so nothing that has a page.js pays anything - measured: 317 / 369 / 281 network requests on /framework/, /framework/core/Page/ and /notes/ before AND after. A second line does the rest of the work: a NAME inside a page.json's children is declared as another data page rather than as a bare name, so the subtree below the root never asks for a page.js at all - the whole made/ tree now costs one fetch per page and zero 404s. assign.outcome:
**A page now says whether it has data, and a directory with only a `page.json` in it is a page.** Six decisions, one core file, zero cost to every page that does not use it.

![Make's history row](5-history.png)

1. **`data:` on a page.** `data: true` reads the `page.json` at the page's own address; `data: { … }` is that same object inline with no fetch; saying nothing fetches nothing and probes nothing. The file's title, icon, description and six words are read through core's own `Page.props()` and merged with `??=` — **a key your `page.js` set wins**, because the file is the page's data and the `page.js` is the page's decision. The rest of the file stays whole on `page.data`. It rides the `child_source` seam built on 2026-09-17, so it is awaited before the page renders and before its children are declared, with no new waiting machinery. *(`json: true` was the alternative; `data` is chosen because the inline POJO form needs the same key.)*
2. **A `page.json` rung in `Page.load()`.** `page.js`, then `page.json`, then the `.md` fallback — no url pattern, which the owner ruled out by name. The import has to fail first, so nothing that has a module pays. [`/imagine/paging/made/notes/`](/imagine/paging/made/notes/) was a Page Load Error this morning and is an ordinary page now.
3. **A `page.json` IS the directory.** A name inside one is declared as another data page, so nothing probes the server for a `page.js` the parent already said is not there: **one fetch per page, zero 404s, no index of any kind.** The site-wide `directory.json` stays — 4.15 MB, seven live readers, every one of them wanting a listing of a directory nobody declared, which is the one thing a `page.json` cannot answer. The census and what could move is in the doc. *(A per-directory `directory.json` written by the server was the alternative: rejected as the second file the owner does not want.)*
4. **Snapshot and log, both.** Every page you make keeps `page.jsonl` beside its `page.json` — one append-only line per edit, `/imagine/cms/json/`'s contract to the character. Make's right pane presses **Check it** and replays the log from nothing to see whether it lands on the snapshot. The history is written before the snapshot; a page with no log yet gets its whole self as line one.
5. **Make over core.** A made page is a core page carrying its own file: `grow()` hands core `data: file_of(node)` and copies nothing, so one function answers what gets written, what the drawer prints and what the live page says. Honest limit, written down: **Make's `children()` seam stays**, because a made page's url is under `make/` and its file is under `made/` — deleting it would move all nine urls. The same file at its file url is a core page with no Make in it at all: two readers, one file.
6. **Reaching a dynamic child.** `await parent.source_children()`, then `parent.children.get(name)`. `source_children()` now answers for *every* page, so that one line means "the children are declared" whatever they came from.

**The numbers.** Network requests on three ordinary pages, before → after: `/framework/` **317 → 317**, `/framework/core/Page/` **369 → 369**, `/notes/` **281 → 281** — a page without `data:` makes zero extra requests. The **18** data-backed urls: same titles, same page counts, zero console errors, all 18 (the eight Make urls gained two links — the doc links I added to Make's own readme). Site crawl of **389** urls under `/framework/` and `/notes/`: 13 failing before, **13 after, zero new**. `made/` is byte-identical to the 2026-09-17 checksum in 7 of 8 files after being written to and restored through Make's own seam.

**Left, with the reason.**
- **One 404 survives, at the root of a data subtree** — `/imagine/paging/made/` is named by a `page.js` as an ordinary child, so core asks for its module first. A parent that knows writes `{ name: "made", data: true }` and even that goes; `/imagine/paging/page.js` is outside this task's fence.
- **Make's `children()` seam** — decision 5's honest limit above; moving the nine urls is the owner's call, not mine.
- **`directory.json` is untouched.** `ext/AITask`'s dashboard is the one reader that could move today, and it needs the `new-task` skill to write one more file per day — a decision, not a refactor.
